title: Because of the War, Because of the Storm

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6, and *porque* from A1 and *por eso* from A2 Unit 5. *Debido a* and *a raíz de* are formal and take a noun, never a verb. With a verb, use *porque*. They are useful when you explain why people move: a war, a storm, a lack of work.

sections.title: Cause + noun
rows: Debido a la guerra, muchas familias salieron del país.
Because of the war, many families left the country.
A raíz del huracán Mitch, muchos hondureños emigraron.
As a result of Hurricane Mitch, many Hondurans emigrated.
Debido a la sequía, las familias perdieron sus cosechas.
Because of the drought, families lost their harvests.
Muchos emigraron porque no había trabajo.
Many emigrated because there was no work.

items.spanish: A raíz de la guerra civil, muchos salvadoreños viajaron a Estados Unidos.
items.english: As a result of the civil war, many Salvadorans travelled to the United States.

items.spanish: Debido a la violencia y a la pobreza, algunas familias decidieron salir.
items.english: Because of violence and poverty, some families decided to leave.

items.spanish: Debido a las remesas, muchas familias pueden pagar la comida y la escuela.
items.english: Because of remittances, many families can pay for food and school.

items.spanish: Muchos niños viven con sus abuelos porque sus padres trabajan lejos.
items.english: Many children live with their grandparents because their parents work far away.

sections.content: *Debido a* needs *a* and *a raíz de* needs *de*: not *debido de*, not *a raíz la guerra*. Before a verb, use *porque*: not *debido a hubo una sequía*.
